daten.titel: Dead by Daylight confirms Terrifier changes after its new Killer's PTB debut
daten.text: Behaviour Interactive confirms The Terrifier changes in Dead by Daylight update 10.3.0, responding to the PTB for new Killer Art the Clown. Read the full story on PCGamesN: Dead by Daylight confirms Terrifier changes after its new Killer's PTB debut

Coming away from the 10.3.0 PTB, we saw how much of a blast you had testing out (and coming face-to-face with) The Terrifier's Bag of Toys! With the release of 10.3.0 right around the corner, we wanted to give you a sneak peek at the Killer Power and addon changes you can expect to see.  The Terrifier – Killer Power Starting off, we’ve made a handful of adjustments to some of The Terrifier’s Toys: Bike Horn: We’ve increased the detection radius of the Horn as we noticed that some players found it difficult to aim at long range. Acid Bottle: The Acid Bottle was a little too effective while looping, so we toned down how quickly it could be thrown, while increasing the duration of Acid Pools to keep the focus on more thoughtful and strategic ricochets and setups. Handgun: We’ve increased movement speed while aiming the Handgun, making aiming feel slightly more forgiving, while still limiting its effectiveness in loops. On top of these changes, we've also increased the duration of Torture, and have made it so that downing a Tortured Survivor with a Toy maxed out on Deadliness now inflicts the Terrified state. This gives the Killer more time to plan out their plays and keeps Toy progres

daten.titel: The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year
daten.text: The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game. Read more

Towards the end of October, we released a small balance patch using our new Backend Tunables system, adjusting The Executioner and The Good Guy. After working through your feedback and watching both of them in action, we’d like to further refine those changes. First, let’s get a quick recap of what the Backend Tunables system even is. Put simply, it’s a system that allows us to put small balance changes in your hands quicker, without having to wait for full patch releases. Currently, the system lets us make adjustments to many of our Killers (we’re adding support for more over time) and basekit values. While add-ons and perks aren’t currently supported, this is something we have planned for the future. Now, what’s changing today?  The Executioner: Increased the delay between each segment of Punishment of the Damned to 0.015s (was 0.001s) Dev note: The previous reduction to 0.001s made it a little too efficient, especially when paired with the Iridescent Seal of Metatron add-on. This is a great example of why we intend to add add-on support to Backend Tunables, because sometimes, basekit changes will end up synergizing more than we expected.  The Good Guy: Decreased the time to Scam

Whether you were able to tune in live (thanks!) or you're dropping by to get a tl;dr, we're here to give you a recap of some highlights from today's community stream:  MMR UPDATE As you may remember, back in 10.1.0, we updated how MMR is calculated. While kills and escapes continue to be an aspect of MMR calculations, they are no longer the only thing used to calculate these values. Now, we also factor in a wide range of actions that help progress the game – think, emblems. Of course, certain aspects of the MMR have stayed the same. Namely, Killers keep their individual MMR ratings, Survivor share their MMR, matchmaking prioritizes wait times over exact MMR matching, and MMR gains/losses are calculated by comparing Killers and Survivors against each other in a match. Since making this change in 10.1.0, we've been keeping a close eye on this system and recently noticed that Survivors' Altruism wasn't giving as much MMR as it should have. To make sure altruistic play is correctly rewarded, we made an adjustment to our MMR system earlier this week (thanks to the adjustable elements of the algorithm), increasing this value. We'll continue to keep a close eye on how this impacts players

daten.text: With the release of 10.2.0 just around the corner, we wanted to take some time to talk to you about a handful of the many changes that will be happening from PTB to the Live release - and a few changes that won’t. We want to thank everyone who took the time during the PTB to share their thoughts, as we always take your feedback very seriously when it comes time to make these changes. A look at some changes Shoulder the Burden Removed the deactivation condition for other Survivors.  Dev note: We understand your concerns around the impact of the condition of this perk deactivating after one use for all Survivors for solo players who cannot communicate. Therefore, we have removed this limitation. This is Not Happening Removed the Great basic Skill Check zone increase.  Dev note: We noticed the concerns about This is Not Happening when combined with Hyperfocus, and as a result have decided to remove the great basic skill check zone.   Dark Arrogance Basic-attack cooldown no longer affects successful hits.  Dev note: We saw your feedback that Killers were recovering from attacks – including successful hits – too quickly on the PTB, which ended up making chases feel too short. Please stay tuned to our Social Media channels for information on future activities. Our Player Support website has a comprehensive article for removing Denuvo residual files from your PC should you wish: https://support.deadbydaylight.com/hc/en-us/articles/52891224375828-Denuvo-Anti-Cheat-FAQ Thank you The Dead by Daylight Team

Greetings, Fog Dwellers. Today we wanted to talk to you about some of the perk changes (spoiler alert: 58 perks are changing) and content that you can expect in the next PTB, as well as the reasonings behind them.Back in update 9.6.0, we added Diminishing Returns to the game. You may have noticed that this feature did not ship with exponential balance changes to accompany it; we wanted to ease players into the change, monitoring the impact on perk selection first, while we watch to see if any issues arise before making further changes. We feel that now is the time. Our ultimate goal is to update effects that bypass or are minimized by Diminishing Returns, and to buff gameplay effects that can safely be affected by Diminishing Returns to allow players to play around with builds and perks that aren’t picked often. Overall, we will have 26 perks affected by these changes. However, that duration was shorter based on how long Divine Light was controlled - similar to how it was on the PTB. Because it can get pretty short, we felt it was safe to further increase it to 0.8s. We will continue monitoring this. Added a 0.3s Divine Light curve window when non-ZealousDev note: The curving has been a hugely appreciated mechanic to the Zealous state, giving opportunities to outplay Survivors from close range. To give The Judgment an edge when outside of the Zealous state, we're adding a shorter curve window to Divine Light. Zealous is still worth getting due to the longer curve window but being non-Zealous will provide more outplay potential.
